title: Accounting for population structure and relatedness in gene expression genome-wide association testing using a mixed-model approach
protocol: Obtain raw gene expression data.
Perform log2 transformation on the gene expression data.
Standardize or normalize the transformed data using JMP Genomics.
Retain transcripts with expression above background levels.
Extract genotypic data after stringent quality control.
Generate molecular properties for each marker using JMP Genomics.
Numerically code the entire allelic dataset as 0, 1, or 2 in JMP Genomics.
Retain markers with minor allele frequencies >5% for association testing.
Save gene expression data sets in JMP Genomics wide format with samples as rows.
Include a column of individual identifiers for merging data sets.
Save gene expression data also in JMP Genomics tall format.
Create an experimental design data set for certain analyses.
Save SNP genotype data sets in JMP Genomics wide format with samples as rows.
Include a column of individual identifiers for merging data sets.
Save SNP genotype data also in JMP Genomics tall format.
Calculate relatedness Âij between each pair of individuals using the method described in ref. 4.
Use autosomal SNPs that satisfy quality control criteria for Hardy-Weinberg equilibrium (P value > 0.0001).
Include autosomal SNPs with minor allele frequency (MAF > 0.05) to generate the matrix of relatedness measures.
Calculate genotypic principal component eigenvectors.
Generate clustered ethnicity data based on genotypic analysis.
Perform principal component analyses on the entire genotypic dataset using the Eigenstrat method as implemented in JMP Genomics.
Retain scores from the significant genotypic PCs for inclusion in the association tests.
Use the JMP Genomics Cross Correlation process to test for Pearson correlation between all pairs of expression measurements and numerically coded SNP genotypes.
Save only hits below 0.05 to significantly reduce computational time and disk space requirements.
Bring the 10,000 most significant SNP-expression associations from this model (~P < 10^-7) forward for two further analyses in a mixed model framework.
Create a data set comprising all expression and SNP genotype data.
Create a second data set containing columns of the relatedness matrix named Col1, Col2,…, Coln.
Include a Row column indicating the row of the relatedness matrix in the second data set.
Apply the JMP Genomics Q-K Mixed Model process to each of the 10,000 most significant SNP-expression pairs.

Fit a model including Baseline, Location, Gender, Relatedness, Significant Genotypic Principal Components, Clustered Ethnicity, SNP, SNP**Location, Gender**Clustered Ethnicity, and Gender*Location effects.
Use JMP Genomics to call the MIXED procedure in SAS/STAT for the analyses.
Generate JSL scripts to auto-generate required JMP Genomics setting files for each model run.
Each settings file should contain parameters needed for a single Q-K Mixed Model run for one SNP-expression pair.
Run all generated settings as a group in the JMP Genomics Workflow Builder.
Gather results into a single data set.
